findings.claim: test_briefing_has_three_parts checks routing with 'docs/' and '.okf/', but the rules part (audience-picks-the-folder) contains both strings, so the test passes when routing is missing. Assert a string only routing prints, such as 'Knowledge in this repository' or 'Verbs:'. Do not use 'Start at .okf/index.md', because the start-at-the-index rule prints it too.

WORD_BUDGET is defined, and the module docstring says the briefing stays within it, but no code reads it. test_briefing_word_budget hardcodes 600, so changing the constant changes nothing. The test should import and assert against WORD_BUDGET.
The state line prints '1 concepts due for review' when the count is 1.

verdict.text: The change does what the plan asks.
`kmctl briefing` prints routing, counts-only state and the packaged rules without their WHY lines.
It prints 424 words on this repository, works in an empty folder and names `kmctl init` there, writes nothing, and `--json` returns one object.
The wheel ships both rule files.
The only real gap is that the r1 test does not catch a missing routing part (f1).
f2 and f3 are small cleanups.
All three are plain fixes, so none blocks.
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: lint, format and tests pass, eval rows r1 to r6 pass, "stamp green: ea737929a3d3be5cc32f8e767f63ee7c23455b6a9d40c5abcb82023aec89d1f3".
I read the staged diff (`src/kmctl/__init__.py`, `briefing.py`, both rule files, `tests/test_briefing.py`) in full.
I ran `kmctl briefing` on this repository (424 words, exit 0), on an empty folder (the init hint plus the rules), and on a fixture with a broken concept file.
The broken file did not crash it because review_due skips bad front matter.
I built the wheel with `uv build --wheel` and found `kmctl/rules/docs-layout.md` and `okf-bundle.md` in it.
Every verb named exists: init, new with five kinds, check, review due, handoffs.
Each takes --help and --json.
`kmctl new` writes the dated log line that the kmctl-writes-the-structure rule claims.
`kmctl init` writes docs/README.md, which the routing names.
Eval rows.
r2: the fixture has 1 concept due (manifesto) and 2 handoffs, and the test compares both against `review due` and `handoffs`, so the manifesto-name check means something.
r3: the fixture has a due concept and handoffs.
r4, r5 and r6 assert their fails_when.
r1 is weak (f1).
Consistency: the help follows the existing --path/--json pattern and has a one-line docstring and an epilog.
This matches ADR 0002 and the manifesto's I3.
Routing names no skills, which is right because no plugin skills ship yet.
f1 (test-strength, non-blocking, row r1): the routing check also matches text from the rules part.
A one-line assertion change fixes it, and I trust that without a second look.
f2 (nit, non-blocking): the WORD_BUDGET constant is unused, and the test hardcodes 600.
f3 (nit, non-blocking): "1 concepts" in the state line.
The work is staged but not committed on loop/briefing.
I left manifesto I3 at "Status: planned" because no earlier ticket updated invariant statuses.
